verses.1: And King Solomon loved many foreign women. He also loved the daughters of Pharaoh, who were beautiful and charming. They were from my own people, and they lived in my land.
verses.2: From the nations that Jehovah said to the children of Israel, they should not enter them. And they indeed will not enter them. Then they will be led by their own gods. But Solomon remained true to love.
verses.3: And he had seven wives, and three concubines. They were all very beautiful.
verses.4: And in the old age of Solomon, his heart became attached to other gods instead of Jehovah, his God. His heart was not pure like that of David, his father.
verses.5: And Solomon went after Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and also after their king Shikhukh.
verses.6: Samuel did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and he did not follow the ways of his father David.
verses.7: Then Solomon will build a temple in that place, just as the Temple was built on Mount Moriah. And the king of Judah will be like Shishak, who built the Temple in Jerusalem.
verses.8: And so, he made for all of his foreign women offerings and sacrifices to their gods.
verses.9: And Jehovah angered Samuel, because his heart was turned away from Jehovah, the God of Israel, who appeared to him.
verses.10: And he was commanded not to follow other gods, nor to disobey what Jehovah commanded him.
verses.11: And the LORD said to Solomon, “Because you have done this, and because you have not kept my covenant and my laws that I commanded you. Therefore, I will take away the kingdom from you and give it to someone else to serve.”
verses.12: But in your days, I will not do it for the sake of your father David. I will not cut you into pieces by your own hand.
verses.13: I will not tear a single thread from all the kingdom. I will give it to your son, so that David, my servant, and Jerusalem, which I have chosen, may enjoy it.
verses.14: And Jehovah created a serpent for Shelamah, from the descendants of the king in Edom.
verses.15: And it happened that David was with Adam in the tent of Joab, the leader of the army, who was responsible for burying the dead. And every living being in Adam died.
verses.16: For in those six days, Joshua will dwell there, and all of Israel will remain there until every living creature in the land of Edom is destroyed.
verses.17: And Adad and the people of Adomi left the servants of his father and went to Egypt. And there was a little boy with them.
verses.18: And they arose from Midian. They went to Paran, and took men with them from Paran. Then they went to Egypt and presented themselves before Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. He gave them a house and bread. He said to them, “I have given them land.”
verses.19: And Hadad found great favor in Pharaoh’s eyes. So Pharaoh gave him as wife his sister, Tahpenes the daughter of Gibeah.
verses.20: And she gave birth to a daughter named Tahpenes. Tahpenes was responsible for taking care of the treasures in Pharaoh’s house. Thus, the treasures in Pharaoh’s house were kept by the sons of Pharaoh.
verses.21: And Hadad heard in Egypt that David had died along with his fathers. And Joab, the commander of the army, had died. So Hadad said to Pharaoh, “Send me back to my land.”
verses.22: And Pharaoh said to him, “What do you lack with me? Why do you want to go back to your own land?” But he replied, “No, I will not be sent away.”
verses.23: And God created Shatan from Rezun, son of Elidah. He ran away from the place where Adonai, the king of Zobah, was.
verses.24: And people came to him. David became their king in the valley of David. They went into the pool, sat down there, and he ruled over them from there.
verses.25: And Satan became a threat to Israel throughout the time of Solomon. He brought destruction upon Israel, and he ruled over Aram.
verses.26: And Joram, son of Nebat, married Ephratah from the tribe of Zeradah. His mother’s name was Zerua, a woman from Almanya. She was a servant of Shlomo. Joram also struck the king with his hand.
verses.27: And this is what happened: Shechem was taken by hand from King Solomon. He built the city, and he destroyed the cities of David’s father.
verses.28: And the man named Jaraham was a powerful leader. Solomon saw that the boy was capable of doing hard work, so he assigned him to work in all the fields of the house of Josaphat.
verses.29: And on that day, Yeravam left Jerusalem. He found his brother, the prophet Shiloni, along the way. He was wearing a new robe. The two of them were alone in the field.
verses.30: And Ahia tore the new cloth that covered it; he tore it into twelve pieces.
verses.31: And He said to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces for yourself, for as Jehovah God of Israel has said, ‘I will tear off the kingdom from Solomon’s hands, and I will give you ten tribes.’”
verses.32: And this one kingdom will be his, so that David’s servants may have it, and so that Jerusalem, the city I chose from all of Israel’s tribes, may be under his rule.
verses.33: For they abandoned me and worshiped the gods of the Sidonians, just as the Moabites did. They also worshipped their own gods. They did not follow my ways, nor did they carry out what is right in my eyes, according to my laws and judgments, just as their father David did.
verses.34: And I will not take away all the kingdom from his hands. For I will make his wife my wife for all his days, so that David, my servant, whom I have chosen, may keep my laws and commandments.
verses.35: And I took the queen from his hands, and I gave her to you as a gift: ten of the sacred vessels.
verses.36: And I will give him one of these tablets, so that it may serve as a memorial for David, my servant, forever. In Jerusalem, the city I have chosen to place my name in it.
verses.37: And I will take you and make you queen over all those whom your soul desires. Then you will be king over Israel.
verses.38: And if you hear all that I have commanded you, and if you follow my ways and do what is right in my eyes, then you will keep my laws and commandments, just as David, my servant, did. Then I will be with you, and I will build for you a house of truth, just as I built it for David. And I will give you Israel.
verses.39: And I will answer David’s seed for this purpose, but not forever.
verses.40: And Solomon wanted to kill Yarav’am. But Yarav’am rose up and fled from Egypt to Shishak, the king of Egypt. And he remained in Egypt until Solomon’s death.
verses.41: And all of Solomon’s words, and everything he did, along with his wisdom, are recorded in the book of Solomon’s words.
verses.42: And in the days when Solomon ruled over Israel, for forty years.
verses.43: And Solomon lay down with his fathers. He was buried in the city of David, his father’s city. And Rehoboam, his son, became king after him.
